newsitem.title: USA: Jury is selected to hear Oklahoma bombing case.
newsitem.headline: Jury is selected to hear Oklahoma bombing case.

text.p: A 12-member jury and six alternates were selected Tuesday to hear the federal murder and conspiracy case against accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh.

"All right, we've got 18 selected," said U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch, concluding the painstaking process to choose those who will decide McVeigh's fate. He is accused of the 1995 bombing of a federal building that killed 168 people, 19 of them children.

The jurors' identities are being kept secret through extraordinary measures, including an elaborate numbering system, and they appeared in the U.S. District courtroom behind a makeshift wall erected to conceal them.

The gender breakdown of the 12-member panel and the six alternates -- which could only be determined by their voices and by non-media spectators seated along one far side of the courtroom -- consisted of 10 men and eight women.

Present throughout the jury selection process has been the tall, pale McVeigh, who faces the death penalty if convicted. He has pleaded not guilty in the April 19, 1995, bombing of Oklahoma City's Alfred P. Murrah federal building.
The jury is slated to be sworn in Thursday morning, when opening arguments are expected to begin.
